name: stats
title: Stats
description: CPU, memory, disk, network and load on the bar, each its own item that stays off the strip until it has something to say, with a popover of the breakdown: per-core bars, the memory segments, every volume, every interface, the busiest processes, and a sparkline of the last minutes. The same facts as rows in a palette.
author: pal

settings.label: Sampling interval
settings.description: Seconds between samples; the bar items, their popovers and the sparklines follow it. A sample costs about 5 ms (the process table, 20 ms, is read every 10 s and every tick while a popover is open).

settings.label: CPU label
settings.description: What the strip says: the share, a sparkline of the last eight samples, one bar per core, or the share and the busiest process.

settings.label: Disk label
settings.description: The startup volume's figure; the popover has every volume.

settings.label: Hidden volumes
settings.description: Mount points or volume names to leave out of the disk item and the palette (a backup disk that is always nearly full).

store.tagline: CPU, memory, disk, network and load: quiet until they are not
features: Five bar items off one 3 s sampler, each hidden by its rules while quiet: CPU from 70%, memory from 80% or under pressure, a disk past 85% or under 20 GB free, the network past 1 MB/s, the load past the core count; amber, then red

Popovers with the breakdown: per-core bars and the five busiest processes with a Kill key, the memory segments (app, wired, compressed, cached) and the five largest, every volume with its bar and free space (Enter reveals it), every interface with its address and rates, the load tiles
A sparkline of the last three minutes in every popover and in the palette's detail pane, drawn in the theme's ink
The strip's label per item: a share, a sparkline of glyphs, one bar per core, the busiest process, the free space, the rates
A palette of the same facts as rows, Enter copies the value; Activity Monitor, the Processes palette, Reveal in Finder, Kill
`pal://stats/cpu` opens the popover, `?palette=1` the palette on that section
No root: os.cpus(), vm_stat and sysctl, netstat, df, ps on macOS; /proc on Linux

stats.description: CPU, load, memory, swap, every volume, every interface, the busiest and largest processes, uptime: one row each, the value as the name, Enter copies it.

cpu.title: CPU
cpu.description: The CPU share over the last sample. Hidden by its rules under 70%, amber from there, red from 90%; `show = "always"` keeps it on the strip muted, or edit the `quiet` rule to keep it in colour. The popover: the share and load, a sparkline of the last three minutes, one bar per core, the five busiest processes with a Kill key.

keys.title: Open Activity Monitor (the Processes palette on Linux)

memory.title: Memory
memory.description: Memory used as Activity Monitor counts it (app + wired + compressed on macOS, total less available on Linux). Hidden under 80% while the kernel reports no pressure; amber from 80% or under pressure, red from 90% or critical pressure. The popover: the segments (app, wired, compressed, cached, free), the swap, a sparkline, the five largest processes with a Kill key.

network.title: Network
network.description: Bytes in and out per second over the physical links (tunnels ride on one of them and are not counted twice). Hidden under 1 MB/s either way, blue past 10 MB/s. The popover: the two rates, a sparkline of both, every interface with its kind, SSID, address and rates; Enter opens the Network palette for every address.

rules.description: Under 1 MB/s either way: nothing to say.

load.title: Load
load.description: The 1 minute load average. Hidden under the core count, amber from there, red from twice it. The popover: the three averages as tiles, the per-core figure, a sparkline.
